page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c4g1.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for workloads requiring dedicated hardware acceleration. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, delivering 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.5 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. Storage is bundled as a 472 GB local SSD, and network connectivity is rated at a 3 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results show a distinct tradeoff between general-purpose CPU performance and GPU-accelerated capabilities. The instance exhibits weak to poor performance in standard CPU and memory tasks, with a single-core stress-ng score of 952.78 and a multi-core score of 2375.81, both placing in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, with large-block read and write speeds falling into the bottom 10%. However, the dedicated NVIDIA P100 GPU excels at machine learning tasks. LLM inference benchmarks for a medium 7B model show top-tier prompt processing at 316.25 tokens per second and strong text generation at 42.76 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance provides access to dedicated GPU resources and local SSD storage without the premium associated with newer-generation accelerator architectures. It is best suited for workloads that can offload intensive computations to the GPU, such as machine learning inference, small-to-medium model execution, and GPU-accelerated data processing. It is less appropriate for CPU-bound applications, high-throughput database operations, or memory-intensive general-purpose computing due to the older CPU architecture and lower memory bandwidth.

It includes a dedicated NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM and provides a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. While general-purpose CPU and memory benchmarks are weak, with stress-ng and memory bandwidth scores falling in the bottom 10% to 25%, the instance delivers strong performance in GPU-driven tasks. This server is highly suitable for machine learning inference and GPU-accelerated workloads that benefit from dedicated VRAM and local SSD storage, offering a cost-efficient entry point for legacy GPU compute.
